headline: Chips Lead, Consumers Lag as Tuesday Session Splits Along Familiar Lines
body_html:
Midway through Tuesday's session, the tape is telling a divided story. Of 549 names tracked, 302 are trading lower against 245 advancers — a modestly negative breadth reading that masks sharp divergence beneath the surface. Semiconductors stand as the clear sector leader, posting a gain of roughly 1.2%, while Consumer and Software names are the laggards, each off close to 0.6%. Energy and Materials are also under pressure, weighed in part by a complex geopolitical backdrop as the Iran conflict enters its sixth month.

The standout mover of the midday is Dick's Sporting Goods, which has cratered more than 27% — a decline so severe it is distorting the broader consumer picture. Academy Sports + Outdoors is down more than 3.6% in apparent sympathy, suggesting the market read a company-specific development as carrying sector-wide implications for sporting-goods retail. Deckers Brands is off roughly 3.7%, adding to consumer softness.

On the upside, Bloom Energy has surged nearly 5.7%, topping the gainer board, while Marvell Technology and Semtech are each up more than 5.4%, reinforcing the semiconductor theme heading into the afternoon. AMD adds another 4.4%. Into the close, watch whether chip strength can offset mounting consumer and software pressure — and whether Dick's Sporting Goods stabilises or extends its slide.

briefs.headline: Sporting-Goods Retail Blindsided as Dick's Drops 27%
briefs.body: Dick's Sporting Goods is at the epicentre of Tuesday's damage, shedding more than a quarter of its value midday in what appears to be a severe earnings or guidance disappointment. The selling has spread to sector peer Academy Sports + Outdoors, off more than 3.6%, as investors reassess discretionary spending assumptions across sporting-goods retail.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Complex Finds Traction Amid Broader Softness
briefs.body: Marvell Technology, Semtech, MaxLinear, and AMD are each posting gains of more than 4%, lifting the Semiconductors sector to the top of the leaderboard with a gain of approximately 1.2%. The cluster of strength suggests continued institutional appetite for AI-adjacent chip exposure even as some desks trim high-running AI positions to lock in profits.

briefs.headline: Iran Conflict at Six Months: Oil Routes, LNG Deals, and Diplomatic Thaw
briefs.body: Reuters reports that nearly half of global oil flows now pass through active conflict zones as the Iran war reaches its sixth month. Separately, Equinor has signalled the conflict makes a multibillion-dollar Tanzanian LNG project more commercially attractive, while the United States is preparing to return diplomats to Middle Eastern embassies following earlier evacuations.

briefs.headline: Markets Largely Brush Off Proposed US Sanctions on Iran
briefs.body: Equity and crypto markets have absorbed news of a planned US sanctions package targeting Iran with limited disruption, according to Reuters. European shares climbed on relief that the measures were softer than feared, with defence names providing additional support to regional indices. Bitcoin continued to advance through the session.

briefs.headline: Bond Market Signals Shift in US Outlook
briefs.body: Reuters flags that the bond market may be in the early stages of resetting its expectations around the US economic trajectory, with yield dynamics drawing renewed attention from fixed-income desks. The development coincides with ongoing tariff friction, as Canada has signalled it is prepared to retaliate against US trade measures without waiting for further negotiation.

briefs.headline: BlackBerry Pivots Further Into Robotics as Fastest-Growing Unit
briefs.body: BlackBerry's chief executive stated that robotics now ranks among the company's fastest-expanding business lines, underscoring how legacy technology firms continue to reposition themselves around automation and industrial software themes. The comments add to a broader mid-session narrative of enterprise technology companies seeking growth vectors beyond their historical core markets.
